tests.criteria: The backend code implements the API contract derived from the PRD: matching paths, methods, status codes and shapes, with no secrets in code.
tests.reason: All 7 endpoints (GET /health, POST /auth/anonymous, GET /products, GET /products/{id}, GET /cart, POST /cart/items, PATCH /cart/items/{productId}) are implemented with matching paths and methods, and none are extra. Public routes (health, anonymous) are correctly exempt from the JWT guard. Success payloads match the schemas: Session {token}, ProductPage {items,page,pageSize,total}, Cart with CartItem fields, and totalCents in integer cents. Error responses use the {code,message} shape via ErrorFilter, with 401 from the guard, 404 for unknown products and cart items, and 400 for bad input. No secrets are hardcoded: JWT_SECRET, CORS_ORIGINS and PORT come from environment variables. Deviations: (1) ErrorFilter is registered only in main.ts, so it is not in the module. (2) The deviceId has @MinLength(8), which the spec does not require, so short IDs get a 400 the contract doesn't define. (3) forbidNonWhitelisted rejects extra fields, which the spec doesn't say. (4) GET /products/{id}, /cart/items and /cart/items/{productId} return 401 from the global guard, but the spec doesn't list a 401 for them. (5) /products lacks a documented 400, and its page/pageSize validation is manual and returns 400. (6) The anonymous endpoint's spec doesn't say what happens when the JWT secret is undefined. These are minor, so the contract is largely met.

tests.criteria: The PRD must cover every capability the original client brief asks for, add no major scope the brief does not imply, have Given/When/Then acceptance criteria on every story, and include non-functional requirements and an out-of-scope list.
tests.reason: The PRD covers every capability in the brief: browsing (US-001), product description (US-002), add to cart (US-003), and cart with quantities and USD total (US-004). It also respects the no sign-in and no payments constraints. All four stories use Given/When/Then criteria that map to the behavior described. The non-functional section (performance, security, privacy, accessibility, platforms) and the out-of-scope list are present and consistent with the brief; the out-of-scope list excludes nothing requested. Weaknesses: US-004 adds quantity changes in the cart, and US-001 adds loading and empty states, which the brief does not state, but these are minor and reasonably implied. Other small additions are the API reference, the anonymous device-kept cart id, and the Android and iOS platform choice. Also, the 'Given I change a quantity' criterion has no matching story action and sits slightly outside the brief. The out-of-scope list adds items such as admin tools, emails, and returns, which is harmless. Overall the PRD is strong, with only slight scope creep.

tests.criteria: The PRD (output) reflects the product brief and the customer's clarification answers (input): decisions on scope, business rules, payments, delivery and returns appear as requirements or out-of-scope items, and nothing contradicts them.
tests.reason: The PRD matches most of the input decisions. Browse, detail and cart with quantities and total are in scope. USD pricing, the anonymous on-device cart id, the 2-second list load and Android/iOS support all match. The out-of-scope list (accounts, payments and checkout, admin tools, emails, order history, delivery, returns) reproduces the brief exactly. It has no contradictions and invents no decisions that override the brief or clarifications. It omits several clarification answers: the US-only sales market (Q4), the fixed catalogue of about twenty products entered by the owner with no customer-added products (Q1), no stock tracking, and the cart persisting on the same phone on return (Q2). Payments are excluded but not described as a later release. It also adds unrequested NFRs (HTTPS, accessibility thresholds, no personal data), though these do not conflict with the input. The missing US-only and catalogue-scope decisions are the main shortcomings.

tests.criteria: The backlog covers every must-have PRD story with at least one work item, each work item names the stories it serves, and no work item serves a story missing from the PRD.
tests.reason: The PRD has four stories (US-001 to US-004), all marked must. All six work items (WI-001 to WI-006) name at least one story in the Stories column, so none lack a reference. Every must-have story is covered: US-001 by WI-001 and WI-003, US-002 by WI-001 and WI-004, US-003 by WI-002 and WI-005, US-004 by WI-002 and WI-006. Every referenced ID exists in the PRD, with no invented or misnamed stories. The Story coverage section matches the work item table. No gaps were found in coverage, references, or validity.

tests.criteria: The architecture, OpenAPI contract and Prisma schema support every must-have PRD story: each story's data and actions have an endpoint and stored entity, and nothing important in the PRD is left without a design.
tests.reason: All four must-have stories (US-001 to US-004) have matching endpoints, schemas and stored entities. US-001 maps to GET /products, whose ProductPage returns name, priceCents and imageUrl, with Product in Prisma. US-002 maps to GET /products/{id}, which returns description and a 404 for a missing product. US-003 maps to POST /cart/items, backed by Cart and CartItem with a default quantity of 1 and a unique (cartId, productId) constraint for the increment. US-004 maps to GET /cart and PATCH /cart/items/{productId}, returning unitPriceCents, quantity, lineTotalCents and totalCents. The architecture covers the cross-cutting needs: anonymous device ID to JWT auth, HTTPS, no PII, and screens with loading, empty and error states. Cart is tied to deviceId, matching the privacy requirement. Gaps are minor. The PATCH endpoint allows quantity 0 but doesn't say it removes the line, which the PRD never asks for. The anonymous-session endpoint, rate limiting and /health are not in the PRD, though they trace to the non-functional requirements and the anonymous-ID privacy note. Empty and loading states are UI-only, and the architecture doesn't say how the cart is created on first access. Overall the design is consistent with the PRD and has no important gaps.

tests.criteria: Every must-have PRD story is served by at least one screen in the design system, and the screens specify their loading, empty and error states.
tests.reason: All four must-have stories (US-001 to US-004) map to screens: SCR-01 serves US-001, SCR-02 serves US-002 and US-003 (Add to cart button), and SCR-03 serves US-003 and US-004 (cart with QuantityStepper and total row in USD). No coverage gaps. All three screens specify loading, empty and error states. The only weakness is that SCR-02's empty state is written as 'not applicable; a missing product shows the error state'. It is explicitly addressed and justified by the PRD, but it is not a concrete empty state, so a strict reading counts it as a minor gap. Smaller details are also thin: SCR-03 does not explicitly show line total or unit price per line, though the total row and stepper imply it.

tests.criteria: The backend code implements the API contract derived from the PRD: matching paths, methods, status codes and shapes, with no secrets in code.
tests.reason: All 7 endpoints (GET /health, POST /auth/anonymous, GET /products, GET /products/{id}, GET /cart, POST /cart/items, PATCH /cart/items/{productId}) are implemented with matching paths and methods, and none are extra. Public routes (health, anonymous) are correctly exempt from the JWT guard. Success payloads match the schemas: Session {token}, ProductPage {items,page,pageSize,total}, Cart with CartItem fields, and totalCents in integer cents. Error responses use the {code,message} shape via ErrorFilter, with 401 from the guard, 404 for unknown products and cart items, and 400 for bad input. No secrets are hardcoded: JWT_SECRET, CORS_ORIGINS and PORT come from environment variables. Deviations: (1) ErrorFilter is registered only in main.ts, so it is not in the module. (2) The deviceId has @MinLength(8), which the spec does not require, so short IDs get a 400 the contract doesn't define. (3) forbidNonWhitelisted rejects extra fields, which the spec doesn't say. (4) GET /products/{id}, /cart/items and /cart/items/{productId} return 401 from the global guard, but the spec doesn't list a 401 for them. (5) /products lacks a documented 400, and its page/pageSize validation is manual and returns 400. (6) The anonymous endpoint's spec doesn't say what happens when the JWT secret is undefined. These are minor, so the contract is largely met.

tests.criteria: The Flutter app implements the screens and design tokens from the design system and calls the API through the generated client, matching the contract.
tests.reason: All three screens (SCR-01 list, SCR-02 detail, SCR-03 cart) exist with the correct routes. The go_router setup has a bottom bar for Shop and Cart, and detail is pushed at /products/:id. The components ProductCard, QuantityStepper, StateView and PrimaryButton are present, and loading, empty and error messages match the spec text. Theme colors for light and dark match the token hex values and are applied through ThemeData and a Tokens class. Spacing, the 48dp touch target and the typography sizes (22/28 w600, 18/24 w500, 16/24, 12/16) also match. API calls all go through ApiClient with correct endpoints, methods, query parameters and bodies for listProducts, getProduct, getCart, addCartItem and updateCartItemQuantity. Models match the schemas. Shortcomings: the ApiClient is hand-written Dio code returning raw maps rather than a truly generated, typed client. createAnonymousSession and getHealth are never used, so no bearer token is attached and the authenticated calls would likely return 401. Product detail's error button is built with onRetry but labeled 'Try again' instead of the specified 'Back to shop'. The loading spinner on the detail and cart screens shows the default 'Loading' text. Body text styles such as the price and description are not explicitly mapped to the body token. The ProductCard uses hardcoded 56 image dimensions. Product list ignores pagination beyond page 1.

tests.criteria: The Dockerfile and compose file run the system the architecture describes (API plus PostgreSQL, migrations on start, PORT), and contain no real secrets.
tests.reason: The output covers the required components: the Dockerfile builds the NestJS API with a multi-stage build and runs `prisma migrate deploy` before starting, and the compose file defines both `db` (postgres:16) and `api`. Wiring is correct: DATABASE_URL points to host `db`, `depends_on` uses `service_healthy` with a pg_isready healthcheck, and port 3000 is mapped. Secrets are clearly placeholders (`staging_password_placeholder`, `sk_test_placeholder`), and server secrets come from an env file, matching the architecture's 'secrets from environment variables' requirement. Shortcomings: PORT handling is inconsistent. `staging.env` sets PORT=3000, but the Dockerfile hardcodes `EXPOSE 3000` and compose hardcodes `3000:3000` instead of using `${PORT}`, so changing PORT would break the mapping. The Dockerfile comment says it starts 'on $PORT' but nothing enforces this. The Postgres password is also duplicated in compose and the env file rather than shared by substitution. Prisma CLI in the final image depends on `npm ci --omit=dev`, which would fail if prisma is a devDependency. Other pieces, such as rate limiting config and the HTTPS/HSTS settings, are not addressed, but they are not infra-critical.
